These are the coolest cars you’ve seen on the screen; the ones you could actually drive

No fictional super machines. Just real life badass rides

By Mark D McKee Nov 23, 2026 7:30 PM
Email article
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 7:03
Instaread

One of the most beloved relationships every guy can get behind, no matter what their ideals or morals dictate, is between the action hero and the car they drive. Violence upsets some guys. Gratuitous nudity can rub some guys the wrong way. And while action movies are known for these two things, every guy can cheer for the thrilling car chase or stunt. That means there is a long list of cars we love to watch, and rewatch, as often as possible.

The other night, I had this thought while watching The Bourne Identity. Now, the car he evaded French police in doesn’t belong on a list of famous cars from movies, and it isn’t a cool car, but it got me thinking about which cars should be on the list. So I started thinking about the cars that impacted me, and others. Here are my five favorites…and five (not) cars as honorable mentions.

NOTE: Chitty Chitty Bang Bang, K.I.T.T., and the DeLorean aren’t making the list…these are cars you could drive today.

James Bond’s Aston Martin DB5

You can’t do an article of the coolest cars in movies and not put James Bond’s DB5 as the jumping-off point. Not only is this the coolest car on the list, and the most iconic, but it may very well be the car that all of the others have been trying to duplicate. The DB5 became the package deal. You can’t have a James Bond movie without a kitted-out car from Q-Branch. And while he has done a few other models over the years, there is no one better than the DB5.

Memphis Rain’s 1967 Shelby GT500 “Eleanor”

Nic Cage is one of the biggest names in Hollywood. And in the mid-90s, he dropped an action trilogy (Face/Off, Con Air, and The Rock) that propelled him into superstardom. Once he was a name, he starred in a handful of hits, but maybe one of the biggest of his career is Gone in 60 Seconds. A star-studded cast, but all of them felt like they played second fiddle to the real star of the movie, the 1967 Shelby GT500, nicknamed “Eleanor.” The car had a mythos of its own, making it more of a supernatural entity, if even only in the mind of Memphis Rains (Cage). After which, “Eleanor” became something of a cultural icon.

Crockett’s 1986 Ferrari Testarossa

Don Johnson and Philip Michael Thomas owned the television screens in the 1980s. Impeccable style, campy stories, and all the prerequisites of a hit TV show: Miami Vice. While the series spends most of its time having Sonny and Crockett go undercover to dispatch the worst of the worst from the South’s most vibrant city, the cocaine-white Ferrari never lets you forget you are in the lavish setting of Miami. It is so iconic that The Wolf of Wall Street uses it as a symbol of wealth and status.

Assassin’s 1968 Dodge Charger R/T

While the Aston Martin DB5 may have kicked off the relationship of the car with the action hero, Bullitt may be the movie that established the hero car. The Mustang McQueen drives throughout the movie is one of the most iconic cars in cinema; for this list, I wanted to focus on a different car in the movie. In the interest of not having two Mustangs on the list, I decided on the Dodge Charger R/T. The assassin going up against McQueen in the iconic chase scene drove one of the most legendary cars in history. I also can’t help but notice that the very next model year ended up in Dukes of Hazzard. The year after was in The Fast and the Furious. Can’t help but think this car is the origin of a ton of iconic movie Dodges.

Starsky’s 1975 Ford Gran Torino

I will be honest, I knew nothing of Starsky and Hutch until I saw the semi-parody movie remake with Ben Stiller and Owen Wilson. Of course, in that movie, the car Stiller’s version of Starsky drove was his baby. The kind of baby that nobody would dare mess with. While the love affair between the character and the car was played up slightly for the movie (like a lot of the elements of the series), there was no doubt that this car became a cultural icon. To this day, it is one of the most recognizable cars (especially with the paint job).

Honorable mentions…not cars

While cars are the most fun, there are some other types of vehicles that are just as iconic and fun, so these are a few of my favorite “non-cars.”

Captain America’s Harley-Davidson Street 750

There is no shortage of iconic and legendary motorcycles in film to choose from. Sue me, I am a huge fan of seeing Captain America/Steve Rogers ride across Washington, D.C. or navigate a battlefield on this 750. This one was so badass that his old pal Bucky steals one to get away from the police in Captain America: Civil War.

MacGyver’s 1987 Jeep Wrangler YJ Laredo

One of the coolest dudes on TV in the last four decades is, inarguably, Angus MacGyver. Working for a government think tank focusing on environmental and law enforcement support and mediation, MacGyver solved problems with brains instead of brawn. He got out of tight spots with applied science and a Swiss Army Knife instead of guns. For a guy that cool, only the Jeep Wrangler was good enough for him.

Jurassic Park‘s Ford Explorer

It may not sound as cool now, but this bad boy was all the rage when I was ten. Automated and conversational, this vehicle took people filled with wonder around the most dangerous park in the world. That is, until it was tossed off a cliff by a T-Rex. That wasn’t a sentence I ever thought I would write. Now, your Ford Explorer is only a paint job away from looking like the movie version.

McFly’s 1985 Toyota SR5

Another movie I first saw when I was around ten years old, Back to the Future had a pretty kick-ass car. The DeLorean not only looked awesome, with wing doors and a slick body style, but it also could take you anywhere in time you wanted to go simply by going fast enough. Forget that it was almost always a bad idea. The true badass car in the movie, though, is the Toyota pickup he covets at the beginning of the movie and ends up with by the end of the second movie.

Bosco’s 1983 GMC Vandura

Look, I don’t know many vans that would end up on a “cool” list. But this customized Vandura from the 80s classic, The A-Team is epitome of cool. Just like the man who owns and drives it, it is truly badass. Don’t turn your nose up at a van, it may very well be the vehicle that can get you out of the mess you find yourself in…if you can find it.
